# Railroad diagram syntax (EBNF)

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-railroad/grammar/railroad-ebnf.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Railroad diagram syntax, EBNF notation (R-PARSE-9, D54, D512): the normative grammar of
`railroad-ebnf-beta` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/ebnf/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a
reference parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it.
mermaid@12 decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this
file (DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed the EBNF notation with Langium (`railroad-ebnf.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`, which does not import `common.langium`); the rules below are its token
rules, in its order, and its grammar. The other notations have grammars of their own
(`railroad.ebnf`, `railroad-abnf.ebnf`, `railroad-peg.ebnf`).

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

Three punctuation characters give way to a longer token that starts with them, as in
mermaid@12: `(` and `*` open a comment, `? … ?` (no `;` or `?` inside, and something other than
blanks) is a special sequence, and a `---` line block is skipped. Elsewhere `?` is the
optional postfix and `-` the exception. A name that starts with `title` reads as a `title`
line. Line breaks are blanks: a rule may span lines, and ends at its `;`.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A diagram is `railroad-ebnf-beta`, then `title`, `accTitle` and `accDescr` lines, then rules.
The `YAML`, `DIRECTIVE`, `COMMENT`, `BLOCK_COMMENT` and `ISO_COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are
skipped before parsing.

```ebnf
ebnf = Header { text } { Rule } EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = HEADER ;
```

```ebnf
text = Title
     | AccTitle
     | AccDescr ;
```

`name = … ;` or `name ::= … ;`: a rule, drawn as a track from its name. A name defined twice
is drawn twice.

```ebnf
Rule @Rule = ID ( EQUALS | DEFINE ) choice SEMI ;
```

Alternatives, one of which is taken; one alternative is itself.

```ebnf
choice = sequence { PIPE sequence } ;
```

Terms one after another, with or without `,` between; one term is itself.

```ebnf
sequence = term { [ COMMA ] term } ;
```

A primary and its postfixes, each applying to what is before it.

```ebnf
term = primary { postfix } ;
```

```ebnf
postfix = QUESTION
        | STAR
        | PLUS
        | MINUS primary ;
```

```ebnf
primary = STRING
        | ID
        | SPECIAL
        | LPAREN choice RPAREN
        | LBRACKET choice RBRACKET
        | LBRACE choice RBRACE ;
```

`title Grammar`: the title (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | HEADER | `railroad-ebnf-beta(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `railroad-ebnf-beta`: starts a railroad diagram in the EBNF notation, followed by a blank, a line break or `%%`. |
| INITIAL | DEFINE | `::=` |  | `::=` between a rule's name and its definition, as `=`. |
| INITIAL | EQUALS | `=` |  | `=` between a rule's name and its definition. |
| INITIAL | SEMI | `;` |  | `;` at the end of a rule. |
| INITIAL | PIPE | `\\|` |  | `a \| b`: one of the alternatives. |
| INITIAL | COMMA | `,` |  | `a , b`: one after the other, as `a b`. |
| INITIAL | ISO_COMMENT | `\(\*[\s\S]*?\*\)` |  | An ISO 14977 comment, over lines: from `(` and `*` to the next `*` and `)`. mermaid@12 tries it as the longer alternative of `(`, so it is listed first. |
| INITIAL | LPAREN | `\(` |  | `( … )`: a group, drawn as its contents. |
| INITIAL | RPAREN | `\)` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LBRACKET | `\[` |  | `[ … ]`: optional contents: a bypass above. |
| INITIAL | RBRACKET | `\]` |  |  |
| INITIAL | LBRACE | `\{` |  | `{ … }`: the contents any number of times, or not at all. |
| INITIAL | RBRACE | `\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | SPECIAL | `\?\s*[^?\s;][^?;]*\?` |  | `? … ?`: a special sequence, its text trimmed, drawn in a dashed box. No `;` or `?` inside, and something other than blanks; it may span lines. mermaid@12 tries it as the longer alternative of `?`, so it is listed first. |
| INITIAL | QUESTION | `\?` |  | `e?`: `e` or nothing. |
| INITIAL | STAR | `\*` |  | `e*`: `e` any number of times, or not at all. Postfixes stack: `e?*`. |
| INITIAL | PLUS | `\+` |  | `e+`: `e` once or more. |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. mermaid@12 tries it as the longer alternative of `-`, so it is listed first. |
| INITIAL | MINUS | `-` |  | `a - b`: `a` except `b`, drawn as `a`, a `-` box and `b`. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the diagram's title, the rest of the line (quotes around it are dropped). It is not drawn. |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the diagram, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `accDescr[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the diagram. mermaid@12's one rule, as two tried in order; the block's `[\s\S]*?\}` is its `[^}]*\}`, written so that line-based highlighters read the block as one span. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `accDescr\s*\{[\s\S]*?\}` |  |  |
| INITIAL | ID | `[A-Z_a-z][\w-]*` |  | A rule's name: a letter or `_`, then letters, digits, `_` and `-`. A name in an expression is a reference to that rule, drawn in a square box. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | `"…"` or `'…'`: `\n`, `\r` and `\t` are a line feed, a carriage return and a tab, and `\` before any other character is that character. A string may span lines. |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t \r\n]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | BLOCK_COMMENT | `\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\/` |  | `/* … */`: a comment, over lines. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
